title: Check: Effect of Catalysts on Rate (2)

questions.stem: Enzymes are biological catalysts. What makes them different from many industrial catalysts?

options.text: Enzymes are used up during the reaction
Enzymes are highly specific, each catalysing only one particular reaction
Enzymes increase the enthalpy change of reactions
Enzymes work by increasing temperature in cells

questions.explanation: Enzymes are protein catalysts that are highly specific - each enzyme catalyses only one particular reaction or type of reaction. They also work at low temperatures (body temperature, around 37°C) and are sensitive to temperature and pH changes, unlike many industrial catalysts.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a heterogeneous catalyst and a homogeneous catalyst?

options.text: Heterogeneous catalysts are faster; homogeneous catalysts are slower
Heterogeneous catalysts are in a different phase from the reactants; homogeneous catalysts are in the same phase
Heterogeneous catalysts change the products; homogeneous catalysts do not
Heterogeneous catalysts are used up; homogeneous catalysts are not

questions.explanation: A heterogeneous catalyst is in a different phase (state) from the reactants, such as a solid catalyst with liquid or gaseous reactants (e.g., iron in the Haber process). A homogeneous catalyst is in the same phase as the reactants, typically all dissolved in solution.
